newsitem.title: UK: French scientist warns of human cloning danger.
newsitem.headline: French scientist warns of human cloning danger.

text.p: People may start to demand the right to clone themselves once the technology becomes available, a French scientist warned on Thursday.

Axel Kahn, director of the INSERM genetics laboratory at the Cochin Institute in Paris, said the debate over the possible implications of cloning animals had ignored strong human desires to ensure their genetic future.
The announcement that scientists at Scotland's Roslin Institute and PPL Pharmaceuticals Pls had cloned an adult sheep caused alarm that cloned humans might follow.
Kahn weighed into the argument with a commentary on a World Wide Web page published by the science journal Nature, which also published the Roslin report.

"The debate in the past has perhaps paid insufficient attention to the current strong social and psychological trend towards a fanatical desire for individuals not simply to have children but to ensure that these childrenb also carry their genes," Kahn wrote.

"Today's society is characterised by an increasing demand for biological inheritance, as if this were the only form of inheritance worthy of the name. One reason is that, regrettably, a person's personality is increasingly perceived as being largely determined by his or her genes."
Kahn noted that sterile or infertile people had flocked to take advantage of in-vitro fertilisation (IVF or test-tube) techniques.
New technology such as intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) allowed for a single sperm to be injected into an egg, giving even sterile men hope of progeny.
Lesbians could now possibly demand the right to genetic progeny without the input of a man, he argued.
"The results...undoubtedly have much merit," he concluded. "One effect of them is to oblige us to face up to our responsibilities."
